ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 354 to 462.33; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Canada Business Corporations Act beneficial-ownership registry amendments (Bill C-42, in force 2024). Provincial: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, and its regulations (immatriculation and beneficial-ownership declarations to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec); Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236 to 2245 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO particulars are filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and, where applicable, the federal registry; full details are accessible to FINTRAC, CRA, police and other competent authorities, with only limited extract visibility to third parties)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FATF-aligned enhanced due diligence: automated screening of all general partners, UBOs at or above 25%, directors, signatories and commercial counterparties against FINTRAC guidance indicators, the OFAC SDN List, the consolidated Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Magnitsky Act, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and foreign PEP databases (UK/EU equivalents where relevant). For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced aviation-asset profile: verify source of funds and wealth for each participant, require a transparent ownership chain with no undisclosed nominee layers, and implement ongoing transaction monitoring on Swift-wire and escrow payment rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises du Québec, at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the enterprise name must be in French; a version in another language is admissible only where the French version is given clear prominence in the registry and in commercial use. Names in non-Latin script must be transliterated into French; coined names and abbreviations require a French lexical and grammatical form acceptable to the REQ, and the declaration of registration must be filed in French.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Loan and investment company terms (prêt, crédit, investissement) requiring AMF authorization
Université / Collège / École requiring education ministry approval
Commission / Conseil / Board implying official status
Reserved professional titles (Avocat, Notaire, Comptable professionnel agréé, Ingénieur)
Government-related or politically sensitive terms (Ministère, Régie, Gouvernement)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before expiry, the applicant may file a prorogation (extension) request with the REQ for an additional reservation period. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) request an administrative review by the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal decision under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and (ii) if refused, appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) under that Act. In parallel, the applicant should reserve one or more alternate names and re-file immediately to avoid losing filing priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for registry compliance: the REQ will accept a virtual-office or registered-agent address in Québec as the registered establishment for service of process. However, for ISIC 5223 dry leasing of turbofan engines, physical and managerial substance in Québec is required to preserve Canadian tax residence and treaty access; reliance on a virtual office alone exposes the LP to challenge by the CRA and Revenu Québec under GAAR (Income Tax Act section 245) and permanent-establishment jurisprudence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Medium; approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical inspection or substance-verification visit within the first 3 years of registration. Risk increases with cross-border engine lease flows, escrow arrangements, and intercompany payment structures. The LP must maintain a serviceable registered office and complete substance documentation (lease files, board/partner minutes, bank records, payroll and place-of-management evidence).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2246 (societe en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ, c. P-44.1, ss. 4, 15, 33-40; Regulation respecting the Act (name rules ss. 2-22); Limited Partnership Act, RLRQ, c. S-32.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Quebec Enterprise Registrar, 2050 rue de Bleury, Montreal, Quebec H3A 2H5; online filing through the Cle d'affaires portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration d'immatriculation (Standard Form S-4) filed under s. 34 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Digital filing fee: CAD 0; paper counter filing: approximately CAD 38.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account requirement under Quebec law for a societe en commandite. Capital contributions are fixed contractually in the partnership deed; any security posting is a commercial matter agreed between the general partner and lenders/counterparties.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Corporation subscribes for and acquires its interest as general partner of [LP name], societe en commandite, in accordance with the partnership agreement presented to the Board; (2) That the registered head office of the Partnership be fixed at [address], Province of Quebec, with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec as the competent registry; (3) That [officer name], as authorized representative, execute and file the Declaration d'immatriculation, open banking and SWIFT/escrow accounts, and complete all tax registrations with Revenu Quebec and the Canada Revenue Agency; (4) That all previous resolutions or delegations not inconsistent herewith are confirmed; (5) That the secretary circulate certified excerpts to third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online name index search and 'Nom d'entreprise' decision tool via Cle d'affaires.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run the proposed French-language corporate name through REQ's index to confirm no confusing similarity with existing Quebec enterprises. Ensure the name includes the required legal element 'societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' and complies with the name rules of the Regulation respecting the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Amend the name before filing if the REQ quick-check flags a match.
required_dossiers: Proposed name including legal element (S.E.C.)
Brief statement of activities (ISIC 5223 aircraft engine dry leasing)
Name search printout or REQ confirmation reference
Identification of the general partner confirming name authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit a revised name through the same portal or elect to proceed with a numbered declaration under the LP's proposed name; correct and re-file within the REQ response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: General partner due diligence and pre-formation resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate records of the general partner; optionally a Quebec notary for attestation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the corporate general partner is in good standing, either in Quebec or in its home jurisdiction, by obtaining an attestation of conformity or equivalent certificate. Have the board of the general partner adopt the pre-formation resolution authorizing participation in the limited partnership, identifying the designated representative, and accepting the partnership agreement. If the general partner is not resident in Canada, obtain a certificate of status from its foreign registry and, where needed, an apostille or legalization for Quebec counters.
required_dossiers: Certificate of status / attestation of conformity of the general partner
Board resolution of the general partner authorizing the LP participation
Appointment of authorized representative (power of attorney if delegated)
Shareholder/officer list of the general partner for AML/KYC purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the general partner's status certificate is stale or rejected, obtain a refreshed certificate from the relevant registry, add a sworn translation into English/French, and re-submit the resolution and authorization package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (acte de societe en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties and legal counsel; optional notarization by a Quebec notary for registration or lender purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement that establishes the limited partnership, sets out contributions and profit-sharing ratios, defines the authority of the general partner, restricts limited partner involvement in management, addresses transfer restrictions, and provides for tax allocations consistent with the pass-through classification. Execute in counterparts; the instrument should be dated and signed by the general partner and each limited partner before the REQ filing.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement
Schedule of capital contributions of each limited partner
Consent and acceptance of the general partner
AML/KYC documentation for each limited partner (identity, source of funds, ownership)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signature or contribution schedule is defective, amend by supplementary deed prior to filing; if already filed, file a corrected declaration and attach the rectified deed, with a curative notarized attestation if required by a bank or regulator.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration d'immatriculation with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - 'Produire une declaration d'immatriculation' service on the Cle d'affaires portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in with Cle d'affaires, complete Form S-4, and enter the partnership name, head office address in Quebec, general partner identifying data, business object limited to aircraft engine dry leasing (ISIC 5223 / NAICS 532411), and the fiscal year end. Attach the partnership agreement as supporting document and the general partner's authorization. Submit electronically at CAD 0 and retain the system acknowledgement and attestation.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration d'immatriculation (Form S-4)
Executed partnership agreement
Authorization of the general partner
Proof of name availability or REQ name clearance
Head office address and contact information in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of non-compliance or refusal, review the stated grounds in the online file, draft a corrective declaration (declaration rectificative) or supplementary filing, and re-submit within the prescribed statutory period, typically 30 days; legal effect generally retroacts to the original filing once cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registrations and government account setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec (QST and provincial accounts); Canada Revenue Agency (federal GST/HST and business number).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the REQ attestation, register the limited partnership for GST/HST (CRA program account RC0001) and Quebec Sales Tax (Revenu Quebec), with an effective registration date aligned to the start of carrying on business. If the LP will have employees, also register for QPIP, CSST/CNESST, and source deductions. Appoint the general partner's representative as the filer and set up direct deposit and correspondence preferences.
required_dossiers: REQ registration attestation (extrait du registre)
Partnership agreement and REQ extract showing LP identity
Names and addresses of all partners
Bank account details for refunds and remittances
Projected revenue and first fiscal year-end
Director/representative identity for CRA and Revenu Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, provide the REQ extract and a letter of authorization from the general partner; CRA and Revenu Quebec will issue an assessment of the registration effective date, which can be contested through a formal objection if the evidence of business commencement is clear.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account, escrow facility, and AML/KYC onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or regulated fintech; FINTRAC-reporting institution; SWIFT network.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an operating bank account in the name of the limited partnership and a dedicated escrow/pass-through account for lease rentals. Complete the institution's AML/KYC process by providing the REQ extract, partnership agreement, list of beneficial owners with 10% or greater interest, and identification of the authorized signatories. Configure dual-approval controls for outbound wires and enable SWIFT gpi for cross-border lease payments. Confirm that the bank accepts the general partner's authority to bind the LP.
required_dossiers: REQ extract / attestation of registration
Full partnership agreement
General partner board resolution authorizing banking
Beneficial ownership schedule of all limited partners
Valid passports or driver's licenses of signatories
Head office lease or utility invoice confirming address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information due to the aviation leasing profile, supply an aircraft-engine lease transaction overview, regulatory classification letter confirming ISIC 5223, and a notarized attestation of the general partner; escalate to the commercial banking relationship team if standard onboarding is rejected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada, Civil Aviation (Commercial and Business Aviation) - passive dry lessor of turbofan engines holds no operational licence; verifies compliance of Canadian lessee air operators under Canadian Aviation Regulations Part VI and insurance rules (CAR 706). No manufacturing or maintenance authorization triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no industrial or physical operating permit required for a passive dry-leasing entity engaged solely in aircraft engine leasing without maintenance operations. Optional registration as a non-operating lessor may be noted with Transport Canada for information only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction generale de l'evaluation environnementale.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - passive dry-leasing activity (ISIC 5223 / NAICS 532411) does not appear in Schedule III of the Regulation respecting the application of the Environment Quality Act (REAFIE); no environmental authorization required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered - no on-site industrial operations, wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or waste handling at the LP's administrative head office. Lease contracts shall require compliance with CAR 625 equipment requirements, OEM maintenance manuals, and the lessee's environmental permits; municipal wastewater and solid waste bylaws apply to the office premises only.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local municipality (fire prevention regulations) and municipal occupancy permit for the Quebec head office; building compliance under the Building Act for any premises owned by the LP; CNESST workplace health and safety registration if staff are employed in Quebec; no airport-side or hangar clearance required for dry engine leasing; any engine storage or maintenance would trigger separate RBQ and MELCCFP reviews.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (federal GST/HST and income tax) — portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Agence du revenu du Québec / Revenu Québec (Quebec Sales Tax TVQ and Quebec income tax) — portal: revenuquebec.ca; entity registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the limited partnership (société en commandite) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec through the Registre unique d'immatriculation to obtain the NEQ (Quebec enterprise number). Step 2: Activate the federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1; the CRA will link the BN to the partnership as a separate person for Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Step 3: Activate the QST/TVQ account with Revenu Québec through Mon dossier d'entreprise or the integrated one-stop registration service; if the partnership is a small supplier (taxable supplies below C$30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters), registration is optional, but aviation dry-leasing revenue will ordinarily exceed the threshold and registration becomes mandatory. Step 4: Designate the specified member (normally the general partner) who is responsible for registration, returns, and remittances; obtain and display the GST/QST registration numbers on all invoices. Step 5: File the annual T5013 partnership information return and, where applicable, the Quebec partnership return; maintain the partnership agreement and partner register showing non-resident limited partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; the Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent under ITA section 96 and the Quebec Taxation Act, so no entity-level corporate income tax is imposed; the Partnership is separately registered and liable for GST/HST and QST in respect of supplies made in the course of its commercial activities; non-resident limited partners are taxable on their allocated share of Canadian-source business income and must file or elect under the applicable treaty provisions; no tax-exempt zone regime applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canadian law; entity classification follows the legal form: an LP is a transparent partnership unless it is a public SIFT partnership taxed as a corporation. Available elections include: (i) a fiscal-period election for the partnership (ITA section 249.2) to adopt a common year for all members; (ii) an election under ITA section 216(4) permitting a non-resident partner to file a Canadian return on net taxable Canadian business income; and (iii) elective and mandatory neutralization rules under the hybrid-mismatch provisions (ITA sections 18.2 and 18.4) which operate without a general opt-out; no partnership classification election is available for indirect tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax, 5%) and Quebec Sales Tax / Taxe de vente du Québec (TVQ, 9.5%); combined standard consumption tax rate applicable in Quebec is 14.5%; dry leasing of tangible personal property is a taxable supply of goods (not a service) subject to GST and QST unless zero-rated as an export.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — the small-supplier threshold measured on taxable supplies made worldwide (in a calendar quarter and the preceding three calendar quarters) for both GST/HST and QST; aircraft-engine leasing receivables will normally exceed this threshold, making registration mandatory; a non-resident lessor with a Quebec permanent establishment is also subject to mandatory registration irrespective of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls, no digital stamping or tax-authority API validation exists in Canada or Quebec. Suppliers must issue compliant tax invoices containing the GST/QST registration number, transaction date, description, and tax amounts (ETA section 221 and Quebec fiscal law); electronic invoices in EDI/XML or PEPPOL formats are permitted with recipient consent; GST/HST and QST returns and remittances must be filed electronically by larger registrants, and Revenu Québec mandates electronic filing for QST registrants meeting the prescribed turnover threshold.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A dry lease of a turbofan aircraft engine qualifies as a zero-rated supply of goods when the engine is, under the terms of the lease, exported from Canada and used primarily outside Canada (ETA section 23(1)(c)); the engine must be made available to a non-resident lessee for use principally on international routes or in a non-Canadian engine pool. An alternative ground is the zero-rating for aircraft and aircraft-related supplies under Schedule VI Part VII of the ETA where the supply is made to a non-resident not registered for GST/HST. Quebec TVQ applies a parallel export test: the movable property must be physically removed from Quebec or used primarily outside Quebec by a person who is not a Quebec resident, subject to the LTVQ zero-rating provisions. The supply must not involve any significant domestic use in Canada; routine ferry flights, Canadian stopovers, or installation on a Canadian-registered aircraft will defeat zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (B13A/CAED or successor electronic export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System or the CBSA GCA portal), including the engine serial number, value, and HS classification
Air Waybill or Bill of Lading evidencing carriage from Canada to the foreign lessee or foreign engine pool, naming the non-resident lessee as consignee
Commercial invoice with GST/QST registration numbers and a clear zero-rating statement referencing ETA section 23(1)(c) and the corresponding QST provision
Signed dry-lease agreement containing the export covenant, primary-use-outside-Canada clause, and engine return/redelivery terms
Proof of payment or inward remittance: SWIFT MT103, escrow release statement, or bank credit advice demonstrating remittance of lease rent from the non-resident lessee
Where applicable, ATA Carnet, temporary export permit, or CBSA/customs authorization for engines exported for overhaul, repair, or exchange prior to redelivery to the foreign lessee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec jointly audit export zero-rating claims under the Export Monitoring and Post-Processing Verification programs; if the engine is not physically exported or is used primarily in Canada, the zero-rated treatment is reversed and the lease is reassessed at 14.5% GST/QST plus arrears interest; input tax credits/input tax refunds are clawed back with a four-year normal reassessment period, extended to ten years in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Civil penalties apply up to 25% of the tax or refund misstated, and the GAAR (ITA section 245 / Quebec Tax Administration Act) may recharacterize artificial structures, including circular engine-exchange and escrow arrangements; criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act can result in fines and imprisonment for willful evasion or false statements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) issues the Canadian dollar as legal tender under the Currency Act and conducts monetary policy; prudential regulation of federally chartered deposit-taking institutions rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and AML supervision with FINTRAC. Canada operates a free-floating exchange-rate regime with no exchange-control board, no central-bank FX licensing, and no prior-approval requirement for cross-border capital flows; the Bank of Canada may intervene only in exceptional disorderly-market conditions. Payments Canada operates the Lynx high-value settlement system for CAD finality.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility: Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations since 1952, covering both current-account and capital-account transactions with no exchange-control restrictions. There are no statutory convertibility limits, no profit-remittance permits, and no treasury-style investment licensing for a passive aircraft-engine leasing LP. The only genuine deterrents are tax-driven: Part XIII withholding tax on outbound rents, interest, dividends, and royalties (generally reduced under the Canada-US treaty) and compliance with Form T106 and SEMA/OFAC-screening rules where the Quebec LP is foreign-controlled. The CAD floats freely; the LP may hold and settle in CAD, USD, EUR, or any other currency without central-bank consent and may fund its operations through inbound sponsor equity or non-resident partner advances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, surrender percentages, repatriation windows, or holding-period rules on export proceeds, aircraft-engine lease rentals, or trade receivables. A Quebec LP may retain USD earnings onshore or offshore indefinitely. The only operational layer is AML/ATF: banks report to FINTRAC all electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more within a 24-hour window and must screen each transaction against the Special Economic Measures Act and equivalent UN, OFAC, and EU sanctions lists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CAD/USD) for the aircraft-engine security deposit; Operational Account (CAD/USD) for lease receipts and disbursements
Capital Escrow Account (USD) and Operational Account (CAD); USD clearing via BMO Harris Bank NA
Operational Account (CAD/USD) with USD clearing via TD Bank, N.A.; escrow-deposit capability
Operational Account (CAD) and Escrow Account (USD) via CIBC's US branch network

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD) and Escrow Account (USD); Quebec-native onboarding with direct Registraire des entreprises du Quebec integration
Operational Account (CAD) and Capital Escrow Account (USD); regional strength in Latin American corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium but constrained. Canada does not issue EU-style EMI licences. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud) may lawfully provide multi-currency conversion and payment-initiation services only after FINTRAC registration as Money Services Businesses and, once the Retail Payment Activities Act is fully in force, authorization as PSPs under Payments Canada supervision. They cannot hold or segregate aircraft-engine security deposits as escrow agent for a Quebec LP without a Canadian trust-company or Schedule I banking licence; such deposits must sit at a CDIC-member Canadian bank or licensed trust company to satisfy Civil Code of Quebec obligations and aviation counterparty credit requirements. Recommended structure: a Canadian Tier-1 bank as settlement anchor and escrow holder, with the fintech/EMI used only as a secondary low-value disbursement corridor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid and institution-dependent. PCMLTFA permits non-face-to-face verification only where identity is validated against independent, reliable data sources; in practice, Canada's Big Six banks require at least one authorized signatory (a representative of the corporate general partner or a director) to attend an in-person identity interview at a Canadian branch, or before an approved notary/commissioner of oaths at a Canadian embassy or consulate, when opening a partnership account with non-resident principals. Remote onboarding using notarized and apostilled passports plus certified corporate documents is possible but triggers enhanced due diligence and approval cycles of 15 to 30 business days. For the Quebec LP the bank will further require the REQ partnership declaration, the NEQ certificate, the registered-office attestation, the executed limited partnership agreement, and a description of the aircraft-engine leasing business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partnership controlled through an offshore corporate general partner or intermediary holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate-tower file: certified LP agreement; REQ partnership declaration and NEQ certificate; cascading beneficial-ownership schedule identifying all individuals and entities holding >25%; general partner certificate of good standing and audited financial statements; sponsor capital-contribution trail with bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aviation-sector sanctions exposure to lessees, MROs, brokers, or end-users in sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Programmatic sanctions-screening policy covering OSFI, OFAC, SEMA, EU, and UN lists; lessee and end-user attestations of lawful operation; red-flag indicator review of the entire engine trading and leasing chain; independent AML/ATF due-diligence memorandum addressing each counterparty and country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-time inbound capital injection from a third-country SPV (e.g., Irish or Cayman aviation-fund vehicle) with opaque source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds dossier: audited consolidated financial statements; subscription and credit agreements; SWIFT routing memos; bank reference letters; commercial explanation of the lease transaction; sponsor tax-clearance certificates; Form T106 Partnership Information Return where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow misuse or commingling risk on aircraft-engine security deposits and maintenance reserves
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tri-party segregated escrow agreement with an explicit no-commingling covenant; payment-flow diagrams; quarterly escrow reconciliations to lessor and lessee; FINTRAC EFT reporting for aggregate transfers above CAD 10,000 in any 24-hour period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or foreign-government involvement among limited partners, or unexplained wealth indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declarations from every partner; PEP database screening results; notarized and apostilled identification; documented source of wealth for the relevant individual; enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring with senior-management sign-off.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control permit is required. Sponsor equity should be routed by SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 with MT103 cover, in CAD or USD, directly to the LP's operating account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, with a descriptive payment narrative stating 'capital contribution — Quebec limited partnership — aircraft-engine leasing'. USD wires from a US tax-equity sponsor should clear through the Canadian bank's US affiliate (BMO Harris, TD Bank NA, CIBC US) for same-day intra-bank availability; CAD legs settle through Payments Canada's Lynx system with Bank of Canada finality. Escrow security deposits must be wired to the segregated escrow account with the explicit reference 'security deposit — aircraft-engine lease agreement'. Every wire is screened against SEMA and OFAC lists and aggregated for FINTRAC EFT reporting when the CAD-equivalent reaches 10,000 or more within 24 hours.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended clearing mix: (1) SWIFT MT103 (gpi-tracked) for lease-rental payments, OEM milestone payments (Pratt & Whitney, GE Aerospace, CFM), and commission payments; (2) ICC UCP600 commercial documentary credits for engine-overhaul, MRO, and parts purchases, with a confirming bank in the beneficiary's jurisdiction; (3) standby letters of credit (ISP98) for performance, repurchase, and maintenance obligations; (4) intra-bank transfers via Lynx for CAD or via the bank's US subsidiary for USD to eliminate correspondent costs. Arm's-length supplier payments for goods and services are not subject to Part XIII withholding, whereas lease-rent distributions to non-resident partners remain within standard Part XIII withholding mechanics (generally reduced by treaty). No foreign-exchange conversion, surrender, or Bank-of-Canada authorization is ever mandated for these outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla USD/CAD FX forwards under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex, tenors of 3 to 24 months, bilaterally cleared with a Canadian Schedule I derivative counterparty
European-style FX options on USD/CAD (call/put and zero-cost collars) to establish lease-rental budget-rate floors without premium leakage
Cross-currency swaps matching USD lease-receivable cash flows against the LP's CAD operating-cost and distribution currency profile

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely for incidental third-currency exposures embedded in lessee payment streams (e.g., CNY, INR, NGN); no NDF is available or commercially standard for CAD/USD, which is a fully deliverable onshore pair
Interest-rate swaps and forward rate agreements ancillary to credit facilities, permitted strictly for hedging commercial risk and only with prior risk-committee authorization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the limited partnership's registration (declaration de mise à jour annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RLRQ c P-44.1, including confirmation of the general partner, partners holding 25% or more of voting or capital interests, registered office address, and statutory particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Gouvernement du Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31; the annual renewal declaration must be received by the Registrar no later than March 31 of each year for the preceding registration cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted annual updates expose the limited partnership to an administrative notice of intention to strike off, radiation (strike-off) from the Quebec enterprise register, cessation of legal personality, and penalties of CAD 300 to CAD 10,000 for false, incomplete, or untimely statements; restoration requires filing arrears and paying late/reinstatement charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal partnership information return (Form T5013 - Partnership Information Return), including T5013 slips issued to each general and limited partner reporting allocated income, losses, and fiscal-period items
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for the standard December 31 fiscal year-end, the T5013 return and slips must be filed by May 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties accrue monthly for the partnership under the Income Tax Act (minimum CAD 100 per default, with graduated amounts), and per-slip penalties apply for missing or incorrect T5013 slips (CAD 100 per slip plus up to 20% of unreported allocations in aggravated cases); continuing failure may trigger escalated CRA enforcement action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information declaration (Form CO-17 - Déclaration de renseignements d'une société de personnes) and RL-15 slips issued to partners resident in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Revenu Québec (Quebec Revenue Agency), Quebec City
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, CO-17 is due by May 31, while RL-15 slips are due by February 28 (or March 31 when filed electronically)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or omission of partner information subjects the partnership and its representatives to nominal and daily penalties under the Taxation Act (Quebec), ranging from CAD 100 to CAD 25,000 for information returns, in addition to potential seizure action by Revenu Quebec against partnership assets; no tax is assessed against the partnership itself as the entity is fiscally transparent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory annual audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership by the Civil Code of Quebec or by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; audit is required only where the limited partnership agreement or the general partner's governance documents mandate it, where lessor or lender covenants in aircraft-engine finance or dry-lease transactions require certified statements, or where the general partner is a corporation subject to audit under the Quebec Business Corporations Act or Canada Business Corporations Act; otherwise, a review or compilation engagement satisfies the statutory record-keeping standard.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian generally accepted accounting principles for private enterprises (CPA Canada Handbook Part II - ASPE) as the default framework; if the partnership or general partner elects internationally accepted standards, IFRS as issued by the IASB applies, with aircraft-engine lease transactions accounted for under ASPE Section 3065 (Leases) or IFRS 16 (Leases, lessor accounting; operating lease model for dry leases).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For the annual confirmation cycle, the Quebec enterprise register requires the limited partnership to declare and confirm every partner, including non-resident beneficial owners, holding at least 25% of the partnership's capital or voting rights; any transfer or creation of such qualified interests during the year must be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec within 30 days of the event as an amended declaration, and is then reconfirmed in the March 31 annual update; the general partner must maintain a control-person register and confirm that no undisclosed individual exercises de facto control through non-registered holdings.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-750 per annum for registered office services and commercial agent representation in Montreal or Quebec City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000-22,000 per annum for a full certified audit of the aircraft-engine leasing partnership; USD 3,500-7,500 for a review engagement where no lending covenant requires a full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (Canada federal Part I 15% + Quebec 11.5%; LP is fiscally transparent, so entity-level corporate income tax is not imposed and this rate applies to corporate partners)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Partnership flow-through: taxable income/losses allocated to partners; Capital Cost Allowance: aircraft engines fall in Class 9 (25% declining balance), with 1.5x Accelerated Investment Incentive unavailable for property acquired after 2024; no Quebec entity-level tax for LPs; eligible corporate partners may claim Quebec tax credits and the mechanical/aviation investment tax credit (if qualified activities).
